texto: Purpose (provenance: 03_help/Stata/PIBDeflactor.sthlp “Descripción”): `PIBDeflactor` downloads, processes and projects Mexico's main macroeconomic indicators: GDP (PIB), price deflator, inflation and labor demographics. It is the base command of the Simulador Fiscal CIEP: it produces the deflator and the GDP that all other commands (LIF, PEF, SHRFSP, etc.) use to express values in real terms; the series are presented in three segments (observed history since 1993, SHCP CGPE estimates, CIEP projections with the growth globals of SIM.do §2).

texto: Purpose (provenance: 03_help/Stata/SCN.sthlp “Descripción”; 02_governance/scn-celdas.md header): `SCN` downloads, processes and projects Mexico's Sistema de Cuentas Nacionales (SCN, national accounts), integrating two official INEGI sources: BIE (income, gross output, household consumption, government expenditure and GDP by economic activity) and CSI (accounts by institutional sector: mixed income, social security contributions, subsidies and operating surplus). It allows GDP to be decomposed by its three approaches and the functional distribution of income among labor, capital and depreciation to be obtained; it is an input to TasasEfectivas, GastoPC, Households and NTA. What the engine reads is master/SCN.dta, built by UpdateSCN from the 525 BIE series and the CSI tables frozen in raw/SCN/ (asset scn-congelado-2024.zip; anchors in anioenigh, Package framework from the last frozen year).
Inputs (provenance: CUAD-0 §2 rows “CSI” and “BIE, series SCN”; manifest.json scn_vintage; 02_governance/scn-celdas.md):

texto: [CUAD-1] `Expenditure` builds consumption by person and category from the ENIGH (household expenditure split by `perfilpc`, plus individual expenditure), scaled to the BIE private consumption series by category, and computes micro IVA and IEPS; `TasasEfectivas` takes LIF revenue by tax, divides it by a macro base from the SCN (effective rate) and allocates it among persons ∝ the micro variable of each tax (`ISR_Mod.do`, `Distribucion`), so that the fiscal module, the NTA and the 32 states allocate the same totals.

[CUAD-1] **Gap relative to the template:** `clave_iva.dta` is the only input with no external institution and no methodological note; `clase_de_actividad*` (SCIAN of the last link) determines `va_ratio` and, through it, the IVA and IEPS base.

filas: `recaudacion` by `divSIM` (ISRAS, ISRPF, ISRPM, CUOTAS, OTROSK, FMP, PEMEX, CFE, IMSS, ISSSTE, IVA, IEPSNP, IEPSP, ISAN, IMPORT) and by `divCIEP`
IMSS/ISSSTE contribution tables and LISR rate schedule
IMSS Informe 2021-2022 Annex A.4; ISSSTE IFA 2021; LISR art. 96/152
Macro SCN for the TE denominators

tablas.titulo: Derived from the code: manifest assets (ensure_asset) and products of other modules (use master/)

filas: Joins the four expenditure tables, annualizes (×4), attaches the weight and dwelling data, maps `clave` 2024 → 2018
Assigns `va_ratio` (VACB/PBT from the Economic Census) by SCIAN class of the last link, cascading from 6→2 digits
Classifies each code into 19 SCN categories (`categ`), 11 IVA categories (`categ_iva`) and 12 IEPS categories (`categ_ieps`)
Every code falls into a category (`categ = 19` otherwise)
Separates individual and household expenditure; household expenditure is divided among members and allocated by age-sex profile (`perfilpc`); individual expenditure is added

`perfilpc` preserves the household total exactly (verified); the canonical cache carries `M<k>` = 1.085868 × (hog + ind) in all 19 because `Simulador.ado` deflated the variable in the run with charts of 16-Oct (FLAG 20, §8 bis)
Anchors each category to its BIE series: `TT<k> = SCN/M<k>`; `gas_pc_<k> *= TT<k>`
Micro IVA: price × quantity × `va_ratio` × 16/116 by IVA category (`IVAT`), rescaled to `ConHog`; compared with the LIF
Nothing is anchored: `DifIVA` (23.1 %) is reported and the LIF governs afterwards via `Distribucion`
Micro IEPS (ad valorem + specific rate) by category; gasoline and “sin IEPS” (no IEPS) are skipped; compared with `IEPSNP` from `divCIEP` (24.075)
`TasasEfectivas`: TE = LIF revenue / SCN macro base by tax; `Distribucion` allocates the LIF ∝ micro variable (`ISRAS`, `CUOTAS`, …)
`ISR_Mod.do`: recomputes contributions and the rate schedule with the form parameters; cut-off by probit; hard-coded splicing factors (3.793/3.255, 0.241/0.553, 4.176/2.781, 1.675/1.525)
Σ simulated ISR = LIF in the default (the ratios are calibrated by hand)
`Households.do` §6–§11: contributions by regime (`cuotasT/P/F`, infonavit), gross-up of wages, ISR by rate schedule, three probits and three cut-offs to the LIF
Total ISR = LIF (7.961 vs 7.967 % of GDP, `L`)

“PF ISR liability anchored by declared income bracket (ITAN Q4)”

**Decision 9 rewritten in 8.16a.** The first version said “not published by SAT/SHCP for 2024”: that is incorrect. The *Informes sobre la Situación Económica, las Finanzas Públicas y la Deuda Pública* (SHCP quarterly reports) publish every quarter, in the public finance annex `itanfp02_<AAAA><TT>.xlsx`, sheet “I.II RecGobFed a) ISR”, ISR revenue (million pesos, cumulative January–quarter) by **annual income bracket declared by the taxpayer** (12 brackets, thousands of pesos) × **type** (legal persons; PF with business activity; PF without business activity; withholding on wages and salaries by PM and by PF; other auxiliary items), plus sector of activity and number of taxpayers who filed a return with payment; Q4 is the annual figure (Table 1b, new row; asset `raw/ITAN/itan-congelado.zip`, catalog `05_scripts/itan-catalogo.json`, `AccesoITAN.ado` → `master/itan-isr-rangos.dta`, 2019-1 … 2026-3). **Methodological note:** (i) the bracket is of *declared annual income* (note 1_/ of the table; RIF via bimonthly returns), not of taxable base nor of ISR due: mapping it to the ENIGH requires assuming that declared income corresponds to the person's annual `ing_bruto_tax` (accruable income before deductions) and that the distribution *within* each bracket is that of the ENIGH; (ii) in the **withholding on wages and salaries** columns the “taxpayer” is the withholding agent (the employer: 584.5 of the 1,254.8 bn fall in “more than 500 million”), so those brackets rank firms, **not** employees: only the PF columns with and without business activity (77.117 bn in 2024) anchor PF liability by bracket; employees' liability is still anchored by total (`ISRAS` LIF = ITAN withholding on wages 1,254.807 to the peso); (iii) they are annual cumulative figures and preliminary SAT figures (the SHCP revised 2021 and 2022-Q3: Table 1b); (iv) “Resto” (remainder) = taxpayers without an annual return (412.9 bn of withholding) and the low PF brackets without business activity come out negative (refunds): the anchor by bracket is built on the 11 brackets with PF ≥ 0 and “Resto” is allocated ∝ ENIGH, declared. With `enigh` liability by bracket is not anchored (current).

`corte` (current): formal = those with the highest *p* until Σ liability = LIF revenue (`H l.2438–2439`). `probabilistica`: expected payment = λ·*p*·liability over the whole base (λ = collected / Σ *p*·liability = 1.1666 in v8.15.3). [CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] One entry per finding of the CUAD-1 report: where (file and lines in `9b1c758`), mechanism (economics, not Stata), since when (`git log -S` / `git blame`; “predates the repo” = it was already in the first upload of 2018-10-29), how much it weighs (bn 2024 and keys of `output.txt`), proposed correction and its type. Nothing is corrected here; the figures come from the `.dta` files of `-datos` (pandas, `probes/`) and from three runs in disposable worktrees (`diag-8.16a-2026-11-07/`): R0 (`PIBDeflactor`), R1 (`Expenditure.do` without cache and without graphs) and R2 (full `SIM.do` with `isras_share = acotado`).

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 1 — FLAG 20: consumption ×1.085868 uniform.** 1. *Where.* `Simulador.ado` l. 109, inside the graphing routine: `replace `varlist' = `varlist'/`deflator'` (no `if`, no `restore`), with `deflator` = `PIBDeflactor, anio(aniovp)` and `aniovp` = the **calendar year of the run** when it is not passed (l. 64–66). `Expenditure.do` l. 801 (`noisily Simulador o`vars'pc_`k' … aniope(`anioenigh') …`) and l. 830 (`gas_pc_`k'`), only when `$nographs` is empty. The cache `master/2024/consumption_*_pc.dta` is built once (§3, guard `capture confirm file`) and nobody regenerates it afterwards. 2. *Mechanism.* The routine that draws the profiles expresses the variable in pesos of the present-value year by dividing it by the deflator, and it does so on the variable itself, not on a copy. The intra-household split (`perfilpc`) preserves household expenditure exactly (verified: residual ≤ 0.0003 bn in the 19 categories), so the whole jump is the deflator: `1/deflactor_2024` with base 2026 = `1/0.920922131` = **1.085868139** (R0, with the globals `def2026 = 3.8` of `SIM.do`; with base 2027 it would be 1.1293 and with 2025, 1.0461: the constant depends on the date of the run). That is why `ogas_pc_<k>` = 1.085868 × `gas_hog<k>` in the same record (the “original” copy was already deflated) and Σ gas_pc = 1.085868 × (hog + ind) to the peso. 3. *Since when.* The `replace` in `Simulador.ado` exists since `cda5c1d` (2023-03-28, v5.5); the call in `Expenditure.do` on `ogas_pc` since `0afac4e` (2025-09-02, ENIGH 2024; `perfilpc` kept it in `4eba8a7`, 2026-10-03). [CUAD-0 · §10 bis — Verification against the manual (sign-off v3 §D, 2026-10-31; verbatim paragraphs, page and URL)] 1. **Households' actual rents → B.3n (decision 3; `rentas_celda = b3n`): green.** SNA 2008 §7.9: “In practice, all unincorporated enterprises owned by households that are not quasi-corporations are deemed to have mixed income as their balancing item, except owner-occupiers in their capacity as producers of housing services for own final consumption and households employing paid domestic staff. For owner-occupiers, all value added is operating surplus and for domestic staff all value added is compensation of employees.” §7.19(c): “The balance of primary incomes of the household sector consists of compensation of employees and mixed incomes accruing to households, plus property income receivable less property income payable. It also includes the operating surplus from housing services produced for own consumption by owner-occupiers.” INEGI, p. 33 (our translation): “…the surplus arising from the productive activities of an unincorporated enterprise belonging to a household represents a combination of two different kinds of income, which is why the current SCN calls it ‘Mixed income’ instead of ‘operating surplus’, except in the case of the surplus arising from own-account production of housing services.” INEGI, p. 45: “In the case of Households, the surplus originates in the own-account production of the dwelling rental service.” B.2n S.14 = imputed rent and nothing else; a landlord's actual rents are B.3n. 2. **Businesses P068–P081 wholly to B.3n: green with a quasi-corporations FLAG.** INEGI, p. 12: “‘Quasi-corporations’ are enterprises that are not incorporated but operate as such, since they behave autonomously and independently of their owners and have complete sets of accounts, a necessary condition for them to be treated as quasi-corporations. As a consequence, quasi-corporations owned by Households or by Government are grouped together with non-financial corporations”. INEGI, p. 33: “…own-account workers, independent professionals, ejidatarios, day laborers, artisans, street vendors, etc. are also counted as producer households.” The ENIGH does not identify quasi-corporations; the coverage (Σ raw / B.3n) is declared as a factor with a FLAG. Yellow seal only because of that FLAG. 3. **Neutral D.442/D.614 circuit (decision 11): green.** INEGI, p. 46: “Investment income payable on pension entitlements (D.442) comprises the returns obtained from investing the pension funds, which are owned by the workers and managed by some institution, usually a financial one”. INEGI, p. 47: “Households' social contribution supplements are the property income earned during the accounting period on the stock of pension and non-pension entitlements.” SNA 2008 ch. 8 (draft §8.77, §8.83): the supplements “represent the return to the pension fund of the property income earned on the start of year pension entitlement”. CSI_115: D.442 = D.614 = 605.932 to the peso (f.103, f.127). 4. **D.8: green.** INEGI, p. 49: “The Adjustment for the change in pension entitlements (D.8) is a transaction that arises from the difference between the pension contributions paid into the funds and the pension benefits collected by pensioners … With this adjustment the difference is treated as if it were the collective property of the households that have claims on those funds”. That is what `NTA.do` does (`YA_d8` ∝ YL of contributors). No change in 8.15b. 5. **Remittances D.752: green.** INEGI, p. 48: “…between households, consisting of the regular remittances between members of the same family resident in different parts of the same country or in different countries (D.752)”. SNA 2008 ch. 8 draft §8.26(e). Cell confirmed: CSI_115 f.150 D.752 received 1,188.474. 6. **GDP vs GNI — SNA 2008 §7.21** (supports the row “Net primary income paid abroad” of the sector identity): “It follows that the difference between the numerical values of GNI and GDP is equal to the difference between the total primary incomes receivable by residents from non-residents and the total primary incomes payable by residents to non-residents (that is, net income from abroad).” 7. **Step 0 (check to the peso that B.2n = imputed rent): it does NOT match; FLAG 18 is about content, not about reading or vintage (Ricardo, 2026-10-31).** INEGI publishes gross imputed rent in the Cuenta Satélite de Vivienda de México (housing satellite account, CSVM) 2024 (results report 47/25, 21-Nov-2025, pp. 7–8, https://www.inegi.org.mx/contenidos/saladeprensa/boletines/2025/viviendasat/CSVM2024_RR.pdf): “In addition, the CSVM provides data on the valuation of imputed rent, which represents the amount an owner would pay if they rented the dwelling they live in … In 2024, this item reached 1 886 385 million pesos. This figure represented 6.0 % of the GDP of the total economy.” Against the CSI: B.2b S.14 = 2,107.569 (CSI_115 f.59), P.51c1 = 1,197.210 (f.61), B.2n = 910.359 (f.63/f.69). B.2b − CSVM imputed rent = **+221.184 bn (11.7 % of B.2b; 0.66 % of GDP)**; the comparison is in gross terms because INEGI does not publish the net GVA of imputed rent. It is not vintage (the BIE–CSI vintage of GDP is 0.25 %): something else lives in the households' B.2 despite INEGI's text (p. 45); the obvious candidate is actual rents on leased dwellings (SNA 2008 §24.55: “By convention, all the value added arising from leasing dwellings is treated as operating surplus, not mixed income”). Up to v8.17.1 the cell stayed in B.3n (SNA §7.9 + INEGI p. 33, 45): `rentas_celda = b3n`; the other scenario, `b2n`, was measured (`diag-v8.15b-2026-10-31/r2-firma-hasta3`: TaltimirSelf 3.9144, TaltimirHouse 1.9671, same totals of Yl, Yk and Σ S, different distribution). **CUAD-3 (2026-11-08) closes FLAG 18 with `b2n`:** del Castillo (CEPAL LC/TS.2023/44, p. 232) writes that “the System of National Accounts includes, under item B.2b Gross operating surplus of the Households sector (S.14), the rent from real estate, plus the imputed rent of the dwellings that families occupy”, and his table 69 (p. 233) puts X017 “Alquiler de casas, edificios e inmuebles” (rental of houses, buildings and real estate) in the B.2b group; that is the reading of SNA 2008 §24.55. Paragraphs §7.9 and §7.19(c) and INEGI p. 33/45 speak of the surplus from **own-account production of housing services** (imputed rent) and do not deny that leasing to third parties is operating surplus: too much was read into them. Current support for the cell: SNA §24.55 and del Castillo p. 232/table 69 (`02_governance/metodo/fuentes/S2300345_es.pdf`). BIE series 724611 “04.1 Alquileres efectivos de alojamiento” (actual rentals for housing) = 2,763.650 does not separate actual from imputed rents and is not evidence.

[CUAD-3 · §10 bis — Verbatim quotations (sign-off rule §D of CUAD-0)] 1. **`dC p.232`** (ch. III §3 “Proposed adjustment of the information”; our translation): “The variable compensation of employees, from the Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGH), is compared with the concept D.1 Compensation of employees (II.1.2 Allocation of primary income account) of the System of National Accounts. The mixed income of the survey will be compared with the items B.3b Gross mixed income and D.422 Withdrawals from income of quasi-corporations (II.1.2 Allocation of primary income account). Property income will be compared with the items D.41 Interest, D.421 Dividends, D.443 Investment income attributable to collective investment fund shareholders, and D.451 Rent”. 2. **`dC p.232`**: “Since the System of National Accounts includes, under item B.2b Gross operating surplus of the Households sector (S.14), the rent from real estate, plus the imputed rent of the dwellings that families occupy (owned, borrowed or mortgaged residences), the following procedure will be applied. The sum of the gross operating surplus plus the property income of the national accounts, minus the imputed rent of the survey, is compared with the sum of the property income of the survey”. 3. **`dC p.233`, table 69**, group “Property income”: “D.41 Interest (resources), D.421 Dividends (resources) D.443 Investment income attributable to collective investment fund shareholders, D.451 Rent, and B.2b Gross operating surplus. Minus the estimate of housing rent from the Encuesta Nacional de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGH)” ↔ “X016 Rental of land and plots; X017 Rental of houses, buildings and real estate; X018 Interest from fixed-term investments; X019 Interest from savings accounts; X020 Interest from loans to third parties; X021 Interest from shares, bonds and certificates; X022 Rental of trademarks, patents and copyrights; X023 Other property income not considered above”. 4. **`dC p.237`**: “At the level of national income, 41% of the difference between the System of National Accounts and the Encuesta de Ingresos y Gastos de los Hogares (ENIGH) is due to property income, and a very similar amount (38%) to household businesses and self-employment (see chart 76); incomes received mainly by the highest-income households. Therefore, the adjustment should not be distribution-neutral, that is, the difference should not be allocated among all households”. And: “The adjustment of compensation of employees and of mixed income is not distribution-neutral, that is, an income elasticity of under-reporting greater than one is assumed. The difference in property income and in transfers is allocated only to the families that have reported this type of income, proportionally”. 5. **`dC p.238`**, equations (3) and (4): Factor_i = [Y_i / Σ_{x=1}^{n} Y_i]^{1.75}; Ponderador_i = [Factor_i / Σ Factor_i]. “Where Y is the income of each person (i). That is, the share of the income of person (i) in the total is raised to the power 1.75 to obtain a factor. The final weight equals the factor of each income (i) divided by the sum of the factors”. 6. **`dC p.240–241`**: “according to the original survey figure (unadjusted), the labor income (wages, Christmas bonus, premiums and bonuses) of directors and officials of the private financial sector in 2018 was 53,000 pesos a month, an extremely low amount. With the adjustment carried out the figure rises to 282,000 pesos a month (see table 74). According to the firm PageGroup, the compensation of a chief executive officer (Chief Executive Officer, CEO) was in the range of 160,000 to 585,000 pesos a month in 2018”. “the adjustment carried out can be considered plausible and slightly conservative; the income under-reporting elasticity is probably somewhat higher”. 7. **`dC p.241`**: “Taxable income is estimated for subordinate employees and workers who had an employment contract […], equal to 85% of their adjusted labor income. 15% is deducted to exclude non-taxed income as well as social contributions”. 8. **`dC p.225`** (Altimir): “Under-recording in each type of income is proportional to earnings, except for property income; in this case the difference is concentrated in the top quintile of the distribution. […] Altimir opted for the most conservative hypothesis, that is, assuming that under-reporting is proportional to income (Altimir, 1975, 1982 and 1987)”. 9. **SNA 2008 §24.55** (already in CUAD-0 §10 bis 7): “By convention, all the value added arising from leasing dwellings is treated as operating surplus, not mixed income”.

capitulos.proposito: [CUAD-0] Builds income and fiscal variables per person and by source from the ENIGH, scaled to national accounts by income type (in 8.15, cell by cell to the SCN of the household sector), so that all downstream modules distribute over the same base. [CUAD-3] Scale ENIGH per-person income to the household-sector cells of the SCN **without assuming that under-reporting is proportional to income**: the cell fixes the total (principle C), the elasticity ε fixes how the gap is distributed within the cell, and the external calibration (ITAN) fixes ε. It leaves `NTA.do`, `PerfilesSim.do`, `TasasEfectivas` and the Sankeys the same per-person base as always, with a different upper tail.

limites.texto: the base of personas morales (legal entities; ing_bruto_tpm) is today the own businesses (P068-P081), which are taxed as PF (business activity); PM ISR is a corporate tax and its incidence on persons must go ∝ d4_relativo (rule P of CUAD-0 Table 2). and ImpNetProduccion (D.29 − D.39 BIE ∝ ing_bruto_tax + ing_bruto_tpm) are distributed explicitly in §12, outside Yl/Yk. (− D.442); components of ing_mixto = aggregate; Σ Yl = D.1 + 2/3 B.3n; Σ Yk − CCF = YAHogS14 (− D.442); GDP identity (BIE) = YL + YA + D.442 + B.5n S.11 + S.12 + B.5n S.13 + B.5n S.15 + CCF + net primary income paid abroad + BIE−CSI vintage (output.txt: CUADRATURA). Seal of the S.14 anchors: yellow (declared BIE vs CSI vintage). (S.13 -> IMSS/ISSSTE), not contributions by persons: they are removed from cuotasTPF (§6). cuotasRCV (retirement: Afores, S.12), cuotasViv (Infonavit/FOVISSSTE, S.12) and cuotasSeg (social insurance: S.13) travel to NTA.do, which distributes D.61 by receiving sector (CSI f.117 R/P of S.13, S.12, S.11, S.15). Alternative off (all to government, v8.15.3). incidence on persons follows rule P (Distribucion ∝ ing_d4_rel, §11.3); own businesses (ing_bruto_tpm, P068-P081) are taxed as PF with business activity: they enter the tariff base (§10.1) and the PF probit. TasasEfectivas uses B.2n S.11 + S.12 (net operating surplus of corporations; sign-off, decision 7 corrected 2026-11-08) as the denominator of ISRPMTE. Alternative negocios (ing_bruto_tpm × 30 %, v8.15.3). with libre (v8.15.3) the median was 1.150 (gross-up vs contributions) with extremes of ±thousands. (up to v8.15.3 formal_asalariados was computed but not used). probabilistica (λ·p·obligation) is not implemented. Σ obligation(formal) − LIF (scalar ISRASSubreporte) is, since CUAD-3 §4 (8.17.2), the IDENTIFIABLE EVASION if it comes out ≥ 0 (FLAG 27 closed; it enters the four-component table of CUAD-1 §4 bis) and, if it remains < 0 with the signed ε, it is declared as residual under-reporting with a RED SEAL. TasasEfectivas/PerfilesSim distribute the LIF ∝ ISR_asalariados of formal workers. texto: Purpose (provenance: this header l. 3–4 and 41–44; CUAD-2 §1): NTA.do — National Transfer Account by individual (Lee–Mason), closed by age group and by five-year age group×sex; it satisfies, per person, per group and at the national level, the identity C − YL − ImpProd = (τ⁺ − τ⁻) + (YA − S) and emits the account, the Sankey of the whole economy (v4) and the group × sex panel published at /NTA.

[CUAD-2] Draw the whole GDP (BIE) as a flow from persons by age → institutional sectors → persons by age, with the INBD as the single pivot and each sector item either with a declared rule to persons or with its own node, so that each sector's consumption, taxes, transfers and saving reconcile with the CSI 2024 and with the `CUADRATURA` of `output.txt`.
Inputs — WHAT IT READS (nothing is built per person that does not already exist in the engine; what is missing is a parameter + FLAG):

texto: Procedure — CONVENTIONS (signed decisions NTA-1 and NTA-1b; not reopened here): how each term of the identity is built:
C          = private consumption at PURCHASERS' PRICES (gas_pc_*, anchored to ConHog) + gasto_anualComprasN (the engine's
correction for net purchases by non-residents: C is that of residents) + INDIVIDUAL public consumption = D.63
(SerEGob with the enrollment profile of PerfilesSim.do l. 365-443, SaluGob ∝ gas_pc_SaluT, other individual items per
capita) + COLLECTIVE public consumption = ConGob − D.63 per capita to all persons (no age dimension).
τ⁻ public = what households pay in S.14: personal income ISR (wage earners with withholding + PF, LIF), social security
contributions (cuotasTP + infonavit only once; anchor nta_cuotas: D.61 − D.614 of S.14 | LIF CUOTAS) and
indirect taxes anchored to the LIF (IVA, IEPS, ISAN, imports). OUTSIDE: ISR_PM and OTROSK (paid by corporations
in the SCN); they are computed and reported (TmenFuera) without being subtracted from anyone.
ImpProd    = ImpNetosProd (D.21 − D.31 of the total economy) ∝ Cpriv: what each person pays. It enters as income; the ImpNet that
Altimir embedded in Yk and Yl (ImpNetProductos_mixK/_soc/_hog, Households.do l. 2420-2427) is removed from YA
(_soc, _hog and ⅓ of _mixK) and from YL (⅔ of _mixK: v8.14) so it is not counted twice. Thus the indirect taxes in τ⁻ are no longer
a double subtraction. D.29 − D.39 remains in Yl/Yk (FLAG).
YL         = engine Yl (v8.15b, CUAD-0 sign-off: Yl = D.1 S.14 + 2/3 B.3n to the peso). The corrections that compensated for the engine up to
v8.14 (pensions × TaltimirSal, 2/3 of the transfers and financial flows of ing_mixto, 2/3 of ImpNetProductos_mixK,
+ ing_suborROW) remain wired in but equal 0 with the signed parameters (pensiones_en_yl = off, ing_mixto_depurado =
transf_negocios, no embedded taxes, suborrow = off) and are reported; with the alternatives (base v8.14) they act again.
YA         = YA_base + YA_d8 [+ YA_ajuste only with nta_anclaS = aditivo]. YA_motor = Yk − depreciation (CapFij: NET base, consistent
with S = B.8n) + imputed rent reassigned to the household head (income) [− embedded ImpNet − 1/3 transf + ing_capitalROW:
0 with the sign-off]. YA_base = YA_motor × fYA, fYA = (YAHogS14 − D.442 with cuotas_d614 = neto) / Σ YA_motor with nta_YA = S14:
since v8.15b the engine already delivers Yk − CCF = YAHogS14 − D.442 to the peso, so fYA = 1.0000 and it is required to 1e-9 (FLAG if not).
YA_d8 = D.8 ∝ YL of those who contribute (nta_d8).
τ⁺ public = CASH: contributory pensions and Pensión Bienestar anchored to the year's PEF (∝ ing_jubila of retirees, ∝ ing_PAM,

capitulos.proposito: Purpose (provenance: this header l. 3–4 and 41–44; CUAD-2 §1): NTA.do — National Transfer Accounts by individual (Lee–Mason), closed by age group and by five-year age group × sex; it satisfies, by person, by group and at the national level, the identity C − YL − ImpProd = (τ⁺ − τ⁻) + (YA − S), and emits the account, the whole-economy Sankey (v4) and the group × sex panel published by /NTA. [CUAD-2] Draw all of GDP (BIE) as a flow from persons by age → institutional sectors → persons by age, with the INBD as the single pivot and every sector item with a declared rule to persons or with its own node, so that each sector's consumption, taxes, transfers and saving reconcile with the CSI 2024 and with `CUADRATURA` in `output.txt`.

texto: [CUAD-1] `Expenditure` builds consumption by person and category from the ENIGH (household expenditure split by `perfilpc`, plus individual expenditure), scaled to the BIE private consumption series by category, and computes micro IVA and IEPS; `TasasEfectivas` takes LIF revenue by tax, divides it by a macro base from the SCN (effective rate) and allocates it among persons ∝ the micro variable of each tax (`ISR_Mod.do`, `Distribucion`), so that the fiscal module, the NTA and the 32 states allocate the same totals.

[CUAD-1] **Gap relative to the template:** `clave_iva.dta` is the only input with no external institution and no methodological note; `clase_de_actividad*` (SCIAN of the last link) determines `va_ratio` and, through it, the IVA and IEPS base.

filas: `recaudacion` by `divSIM` (ISRAS, ISRPF, ISRPM, CUOTAS, OTROSK, FMP, PEMEX, CFE, IMSS, ISSSTE, IVA, IEPSNP, IEPSP, ISAN, IMPORT) and by `divCIEP`
IMSS/ISSSTE contribution tables and LISR rate schedule
IMSS Informe 2021-2022 Annex A.4; ISSSTE IFA 2021; LISR art. 96/152
Macro SCN for the TE denominators

filas: Joins the four expenditure tables, annualizes (×4), attaches the weight and dwelling data, maps `clave` 2024 → 2018
Assigns `va_ratio` (VACB/PBT from the Economic Census) by SCIAN class of the last link, cascading from 6→2 digits
Classifies each code into 19 SCN categories (`categ`), 11 IVA categories (`categ_iva`) and 12 IEPS categories (`categ_ieps`)
Every code falls into a category (`categ = 19` otherwise)
Separates individual and household expenditure; household expenditure is divided among members and allocated by age-sex profile (`perfilpc`); individual expenditure is added

`perfilpc` preserves the household total exactly (verified); the canonical cache carries `M<k>` = 1.085868 × (hog + ind) in all 19 because `Simulador.ado` deflated the variable in the run with charts of 16-Oct (FLAG 20, §8 bis)
Anchors each category to its BIE series: `TT<k> = SCN/M<k>`; `gas_pc_<k> *= TT<k>`
Micro IVA: price × quantity × `va_ratio` × 16/116 by IVA category (`IVAT`), rescaled to `ConHog`; compared with the LIF
Nothing is anchored: `DifIVA` (23.1 %) is reported and the LIF governs afterwards via `Distribucion`
Micro IEPS (ad valorem + specific rate) by category; gasoline and “sin IEPS” (no IEPS) are skipped; compared with `IEPSNP` from `divCIEP` (24.075)
`TasasEfectivas`: TE = LIF revenue / SCN macro base by tax; `Distribucion` allocates the LIF ∝ micro variable (`ISRAS`, `CUOTAS`, …)
`ISR_Mod.do`: recomputes contributions and the rate schedule with the form parameters; cut-off by probit; hard-coded splicing factors (3.793/3.255, 0.241/0.553, 4.176/2.781, 1.675/1.525)
Σ simulated ISR = LIF in the default (the ratios are calibrated by hand)
`Households.do` §6–§11: contributions by regime (`cuotasT/P/F`, infonavit), gross-up of wages, ISR by rate schedule, three probits and three cut-offs to the LIF
Total ISR = LIF (7.961 vs 7.967 % of GDP, `L`)

“PF ISR liability anchored by declared income bracket (ITAN Q4)”

**Decision 9 rewritten in 8.16a.** The first version said “not published by SAT/SHCP for 2024”: that is incorrect. The *Informes sobre la Situación Económica, las Finanzas Públicas y la Deuda Pública* (SHCP quarterly reports) publish every quarter, in the public finance annex `itanfp02_<AAAA><TT>.xlsx`, sheet “I.II RecGobFed a) ISR”, ISR revenue (million pesos, cumulative January–quarter) by **annual income bracket declared by the taxpayer** (12 brackets, thousands of pesos) × **type** (legal persons; PF with business activity; PF without business activity; withholding on wages and salaries by PM and by PF; other auxiliary items), plus sector of activity and number of taxpayers who filed a return with payment; Q4 is the annual figure (Table 1b, new row; asset `raw/ITAN/itan-congelado.zip`, catalog `05_scripts/itan-catalogo.json`, `AccesoITAN.ado` → `master/itan-isr-rangos.dta`, 2019-1 … 2026-3). **Methodological note:** (i) the bracket is of *declared annual income* (note 1_/ of the table; RIF via bimonthly returns), not of taxable base nor of ISR due: mapping it to the ENIGH requires assuming that declared income corresponds to the person's annual `ing_bruto_tax` (accruable income before deductions) and that the distribution *within* each bracket is that of the ENIGH; (ii) in the **withholding on wages and salaries** columns the “taxpayer” is the withholding agent (the employer: 584.5 of the 1,254.8 bn fall in “more than 500 million”), so those brackets rank firms, **not** employees: only the PF columns with and without business activity (77.117 bn in 2024) anchor PF liability by bracket; employees' liability is still anchored by total (`ISRAS` LIF = ITAN withholding on wages 1,254.807 to the peso); (iii) they are annual cumulative figures and preliminary SAT figures (the SHCP revised 2021 and 2022-Q3: Table 1b); (iv) “Resto” (remainder) = taxpayers without an annual return (412.9 bn of withholding) and the low PF brackets without business activity come out negative (refunds): the anchor by bracket is built on the 11 brackets with PF ≥ 0 and “Resto” is allocated ∝ ENIGH, declared. With `enigh` liability by bracket is not anchored (current).
“formality by ranking cut; alternative p × liability”

`corte` (current): formal = those with the highest *p* until Σ liability = LIF revenue (`H l.2438–2439`). `probabilistica`: expected payment = λ·*p*·liability over the whole base (λ = collected / Σ *p*·liability = 1.1666 in v8.15.3). It changes the concentration of payment (top-10 % 47.8 → 57.6 % in 4c) and the number of persons who pay (32.8 → 49.3 M). *p_i* is the probability of being formal estimated by the probit in `H l.2384–2388`: an aggregate reading (expectation); it does not identify who pays.
“the cut is anchored to N external formal workers; the gap with the LIF is declared as evasion”

With `ninguna` the cut closes revenue and evasion is 0 by construction. With an external anchor the cut is set at N persons and the difference Σ liability(formal) − LIF is the intensive margin (Table 4c-extended): `sat` 51.86 M → informality 0.000, “evasion” +170.542; `imss` 25.50 M → informality 294.590, evasion −124.048; `enoe` 23.5 M → 339.692, −169.150. The last two come out negative: the liability the engine computes for contributors does not reach the LIF (Summary 6).

`E l.109` takes `r(IEPS__no_petrolero_)` from `LIF, by(divCIEP)` = 24.075 (without “IEPS (salud)” 200.705); `TasasEfectivas` uses `IEPSNP` from `divSIM` = 224.780. With `divsim`, `DifIEPSNP` goes from 15.0 % to a deficit of 87 % (micro 28.3 vs 224.780): micro IEPS is incomplete (gasoline is skipped, l. 1282) and the display was hiding it.
“IEPS allocated ∝ the variable of the taxed good”

`N l.534–535`: `nta_IEPSNP ∝ gas_pc_BebA` and `nta_IEPSP ∝ gas_pc_Vehi`. `micro`: ∝ `IEPS` from `consumption_categ_ieps.dta` (by category) and ∝ `gas_pc_Gasolinas + gas_pc_Combustibles` (as in `TM l.136–137`). It moves the incidence by decile and age of 628.364 bn.

`H l.2433`: `ISR_asalariados = ISR × ing_subor/(ing_bruto_tax − cuotasTPF)`; the ratio has median 1.150, p75 1.220, minimum −1,395.8 and maximum 7,252.1 in the probit base (`D`): the “wage share” exceeds total ISR in three quarters of the base. `acotado`: clip to [0, 1] (or `ISR × ing_subor/ing_bruto_tax`). It changes Σ liability (1,424.327 today) and therefore the threshold and the counts of §4 bis.

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] One entry per finding of the CUAD-1 report: where (file and lines in `9b1c758`), mechanism (economics, not Stata), since when (`git log -S` / `git blame`; “predates the repo” = it was already in the first upload of 2018-10-29), how much it weighs (bn 2024 and keys of `output.txt`), proposed correction and its type. Nothing is corrected here; the figures come from the `.dta` files of `-datos` (pandas, `probes/`) and from three runs in disposable worktrees (`diag-8.16a-2026-11-07/`): R0 (`PIBDeflactor`), R1 (`Expenditure.do` without cache and without graphs) and R2 (full `SIM.do` with `isras_share = acotado`).

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 1 — FLAG 20: consumption ×1.085868 uniform.** 1. *Where.* `Simulador.ado` l. 109, inside the graphing routine: `replace `varlist' = `varlist'/`deflator'` (no `if`, no `restore`), with `deflator` = `PIBDeflactor, anio(aniovp)` and `aniovp` = the **calendar year of the run** when it is not passed (l. 64–66). `Expenditure.do` l. 801 (`noisily Simulador o`vars'pc_`k' … aniope(`anioenigh') …`) and l. 830 (`gas_pc_`k'`), only when `$nographs` is empty. The cache `master/2024/consumption_*_pc.dta` is built once (§3, guard `capture confirm file`) and nobody regenerates it afterwards. 2. *Mechanism.* The routine that draws the profiles expresses the variable in pesos of the present-value year by dividing it by the deflator, and it does so on the variable itself, not on a copy. The intra-household split (`perfilpc`) preserves household expenditure exactly (verified: residual ≤ 0.0003 bn in the 19 categories), so the whole jump is the deflator: `1/deflactor_2024` with base 2026 = `1/0.920922131` = **1.085868139** (R0, with the globals `def2026 = 3.8` of `SIM.do`; with base 2027 it would be 1.1293 and with 2025, 1.0461: the constant depends on the date of the run). That is why `ogas_pc_<k>` = 1.085868 × `gas_hog<k>` in the same record (the “original” copy was already deflated) and Σ gas_pc = 1.085868 × (hog + ind) to the peso. 3. *Since when.* The `replace` in `Simulador.ado` exists since `cda5c1d` (2023-03-28, v5.5); the call in `Expenditure.do` on `ogas_pc` since `0afac4e` (2025-09-02, ENIGH 2024; `perfilpc` kept it in `4eba8a7`, 2026-10-03). The canonical cache of `-datos` is from 2026-10-16 02:45 (run with graphs, before v8.10.0); later runs (`nographs`) reuse it. 4. *How much it weighs.* **0.000 bn in what is published**: the factor is uniform and `TT<k>` absorbs it; R1 (cache regenerated without graphs) leaves `gas_pc_*` anchored, micro IVA and the 19 Σ identical to 1e-15. In the log: Σ engine 11,026.332 → 10,154.393 (`ETotPIB` 32.751 → 30.161 % of GDP), `TT<k>` ×1.085868 (`TTConHog` 2.1940 → 2.3824, `TTBebA` 12.17 → 13.21), `DifIEPSNP` 15.0 → 14.8 % (the quantities were deflated too: micro IEPS 28.308 → 28.268 bn, it does not reach `output.txt`). Keys: none (`INGRESOS`, `GASTOS`, `INCD*`, `TE*` unchanged). 5. *Correction.* `Simulador.ado`: work on a `tempvar` (or restore the variable on exit) and have `Expenditure.do` regenerate `consumption_*_pc.dta` (`global update` already deletes them). **Code correction with no effect on published numbers**: it moves neither `data_updated` nor `baseline`; it enters in 8.16b together with the new cache in `-datos`. Side note: the first version of this memo underestimated Σ ENIGH by 293.933 bn because `preconsumption.dta` carries an empty factor in the 88,626 rows of `gastotarjetas` (19,464) and `erogaciones` (69,162); today `append` + `merge` in Stata match them all (0 unmatched: the October cache has a cause that cannot be reproduced without rebuilding `preconsumption.dta`, ~1 h) and the engine recovers the factor in §3.3, so those 293.933 bn **are** in the base (FLAG 33: decide whether card spending is consumption).

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 2 — Non-oil IEPS compared against 24.075 instead of 224.780.** 1. *Where.* `Expenditure.do` l. 120–124: `LIF, anio(`anioenigh') by(divCIEP)` and `local IEPSNP = r(IEPS__no_petrolero_)`; `TasasEfectivas.ado` l. 34–40 uses `LIF … by(divSIM)` and `IEPSNP`. 2. *Mechanism.* The `divCIEP` classification of the LIF splits IEPS in three: oil (403.584), “non-oil” (24.075: telecommunications, gambling, pesticides…) and **“health”** (200.705: alcoholic beverages, beer, tobacco, flavored beverages, high-calorie foods); `divSIM` combines the last two into `IEPSNP` = 224.780. The micro IEPS of `Expenditure.do` (alcohol, tobacco, beverages, foods) is almost all “health”, and the display compares it against the group that does not contain it. 3. *Since when.* Predates the repo: the line is in the first upload (`509d108`, 2018-10-29) and survived v5.0 (`36f7a96`) and the refactor `b7a87e0`. 4. *How much it weighs.* **0 in `output.txt`**: it only feeds `IEPSNPSCNPIB`/`DifIEPSNP` (log and `scalarlatex`); the anchor of the distributed `IEPSNP` (224.780, `TasasEfectivas`) is correct. In the log: “informality” of non-oil IEPS 15.0 % (28.3 vs 24.075) → with the correct macro the micro covers **12.6 %** of 224.780 (−694 %): the micro IEPS is incomplete (gasoline is skipped, l. 1297) and the comparison hid it. 5. *Correction.* `local IEPSNP = r(IEPS__no_petrolero_) + r(IEPS__salud_)` or `LIF … by(divSIM)` (parameter `iepsnp_macro = divsim`). **Display correction**: moves neither numbers nor `baseline`; 8.16b.

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 3 — ISR wage factors with median 1.150 and extremes ±thousands.** 1. *Where.* `Households.do` l. 2433: `g ISR_asalariados = ISR*(ing_subor)/(ing_bruto_tax-cuotasTPF) if prob_salarios != .`. 2. *Mechanism.* `ing_subor` is the **gross** wage (with the gross-up of §6: it already includes the worker's contributions) and the denominator subtracts `cuotasTPF` (worker 1.4 % + employer 8.7 % + federal government 0.2 % + Infonavit 2.5 % = 15.1 % of the wage at the median of pure wage earners): the “wage share” of ISR is 1/(1 − 0.151) = **1.170** for someone who only has a wage (median 1.1501 over the whole base, p75 1.22) and it shoots up (−1,395.8 / +7,252.1) when other negative incomes or the contributions bring the denominator close to zero. Total ISR is assigned to the wage with a share > 1, so Σ `ISR_asalariados` (1,424.327) exceeds the obligation. 3. *Since when.* `3322f9d` (2024-06-23, v6); rewritten without a change of formula in `fa13516` (v7, 2026-03-19). 4. *How much it weighs.* Run R2 (full `SIM.do` with line 2433 bounded to [0, 1], disposable worktree, 47 min; `diag-8.16a-2026-11-07/r2-isras-acotado/`): Σ `ISR_asalariados` (statutory obligation) falls from 1,424.327 to **1,238.3 bn** (3.678 % of GDP; R2 log l. 839), **below the LIF 1,253.785**: the cut-off no longer closes, the estimated informality of wage earners goes from 30.51 % to **0.00 %** (the 49.3 M in the base pay) and `TasasEfectivas` rescales to the LIF (−1.2 %). `gate-numeros` RED with **45 lines** of `output.txt` different: `INCD`/`INCD2`/`INCD3` of ISRAS (block 12; decile I 17,579 → 19,509 MXN, decile X 255,040 → 260,137; share of decile X 28.9 → 29.4 %, decile VI 9.6 → 9.2 %), ISRPF (13, ±1), Laboral (15), ImpuestosAportaciones (31) and AportacionesNetas (42); `APORTH*`/`APORTM*` (contributions by age and sex, up to ±0.43 pp), `PROY` of the same four blocks (±0.002 % GDP) and second-order `PROYSHRFSP2/3` (−0.001 pp, −2 mdp); SankeySF decile 10/104 links, age group 4/59 (max. rel. Δ 11.8 %), sex 2/40. `INGRESOS`, `INGRESOSTEF`, `GASTOS*`, `CUADRATURA`, `PIBY` and the 5 SankeyNTA do not change. Reading: the share > 1 does not “create” revenue (the LIF rules) but it decides **who** pays and how many pay; bounding it moves the obligation below what is collected, which confirms CUAD-0 §4.0 C (“the statutory obligation on income with uniform Altimir comes out low”) and leaves wage-earner informality unidentified until there is the anchor by bracket (decision 9) or `ancla_formales`. 5. *Correction.* `isras_share = acotado` (clip to [0, 1], or `ing_subor/ing_bruto_tax` with net contributions on both sides). **Methodological** (parameter + FLAG 27, moves `INCD*`, `baseline` → v8.16.0); 8.16b.

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 4 — Oil IEPS ∝ vehicle purchases; non-oil IEPS ∝ alcoholic beverages.** 1. *Where.* `PerfilesSim.do` l. 288 (`Distribucion IEPSNP, relativo(gas_pc_BebA)`) and l. 294 (`Distribucion IEPSP, relativo(gas_pc_Vehi)`): from there come the `IEPSNP`/`IEPSP` variables of `perfiles2027.dta` that `TasasEfectivas.ado` l. 335 distributes (`IEPSNP_Sim`, `IEPSP_Sim`) and `INCI.ado` summarizes in `INCD*`. `NTA.do` l. 534–535 repeats the proxy (`nta_IEPSNP`, `nta_IEPSP`). 2. *Mechanism.* Car purchases are used as a proxy for gasoline consumption and alcohol purchases as a proxy for all non-oil IEPS (beer, tobacco, soft drinks, high-calorie foods, telecommunications). Vehicle purchases are much more concentrated than fuel spending: decile X buys 37.4 % of vehicles and 19.2 % of gasoline and fuels (`gas_pc_Gasolinas + gas_pc_Combustibles`, Σ 643.136 bn); alcoholic beverages 26.1 % vs 12.4 % of the micro IEPS of `Expenditure.do`. 3. *Since when.* `PerfilesSim.do`: `8c54592` (2024-02-12, v6); `NTA.do`: `d70ef3d` (2026-10-27, NTA-1). 4. *How much it weighs.* IEPSP 403.584 bn: **81.6 bn change decile** when moving from vehicles to gasoline (decile X −73.3, deciles I–VII +81.5); IEPSNP 224.780: **41.7 bn** (decile X −30.6). Keys: `INCD`, `INCD2`, `INCD3` (IEPS columns, national and 32 states) and the age profiles of τ⁻ in NTA; `INGRESOS`/`INGRESOSTEF` unchanged (LIF totals). 5. *Correction.* `ieps_relativo = micro`: IEPSP ∝ `gas_pc_Gasolinas + gas_pc_Combustibles` (as in `TasasEfectivasMicro.ado` l. 136–137), IEPSNP ∝ micro `IEPS` by category, in `PerfilesSim.do` **and** `NTA.do`. **Methodological** (parameter + FLAG 26/34; `baseline`); 8.16b.

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 5 — Gifts between households counted twice.** 1. *Where.* `Expenditure.do` l. 157–160 (`append` of `gastospersona`, `gastohogar`, `gastotarjetas`, `erogaciones` without filtering `tipo_gasto`) and l. 330–331, 335–336… (T901 → `Alim`, T909 → `Vest`, …: gifts given enter through their T9xx code). 2. *Mechanism.* The ENIGH records the gift in the household that gives it (G2, codes T9xx: 90.530 bn) and the good received in the household that receives it (G5, code of the good: 548.144 bn); the SCN counts consumption once. In the anchored base G2 weighs 90.530 × 1.085868 × `TT<k>` = **223.272 bn** (Alim 131.7, RecrT 36.9, STra 13.9, DiveT 13.3), assigned to the giving household. 3. *Since when.* Predates the repo (`509d108`; the T9xx classification is in v5.0 `36f7a96`). 4. *How much it weighs.* The anchored Σ does not change (the 19 `TT<k>` absorb it): **redistribution of up to 223.272 bn** across households (from the receiver to the giver). Keys: `INCD*` only via the micro IVA base (rescaled to `ConHog`), second order; `GASTOS`/`INGRESOS` unchanged. 5. *Correction.* Decision 3: count G5 (drop `tipo_gasto == "G2"` in §2) or G2. **Methodological** (FLAG 22; `baseline`); 8.16b.

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 6 — Predial (property tax) and tenencia (vehicle tax), LP gas and fuels misclassified.** 1. *Where.* `Expenditure.do` l. 338–347: R003 (natural gas) and R004 (property tax) → `Alqu` (categ 7); R012 (vehicle tax) → `FTra` (13); G005–G016 (LP gas 111.599, fuels 10.209, and services) → `HogaT` (10); R001 → `Elec` (9). 2. *Mechanism.* Property tax and vehicle tax are D.59 (current taxes on property), not consumption; LP gas, solid fuels and natural gas are COICOP 04.5 (“electricity, gas and other fuels”, BIE 724614), not “household articles” (05) nor rent (04.1). That is why `TT<Elec>` = 4.91 and `TT<HogaT>` = 3.84 measure classification, not under-reporting. 3. *Since when.* Predates the repo (`509d108`, v5.0 `36f7a96`). 4. *How much it weighs.* Property tax + vehicle tax 53.443 raw → **169.1 bn** anchored as consumption (R004 × 1.0859 × 1.5699 = 51.7; R012 × 1.0859 × 4.6767 = 117.4). LP gas + fuels + natural gas 140.384 raw: if they move to `Elec`, `TT<Elec>` 4.910 → **2.449**, `TT<HogaT>` 3.836 → 6.161, `TT<Alqu>` 1.570 → 1.585; without property tax `TT<Alqu>` → 1.614; without vehicle tax `TT<FTra>` 4.677 → 4.888. Keys: redistribution within Σ Cpriv (no change in the total); `INCD*` IVA second order. 5. *Correction.* Reclassify (decision 15): R004/R012 out of consumption → `OTROSK`/D.59; G009–G016, R003 → categ 9. **Methodological** (FLAG 24/25; `baseline`); 8.16b.

[CUAD-1 · §8 bis — Diagnosis of the findings (session 8.16a, 2026-11-07)] **Entry 7 — +209.212 of D.5: classification S.14 ↔ S.11 + S.12.** 1. *Where.* `Households.do` l. 315–336 (`LIF … by(divCIEP)` → `ISRSalarios`, `ISRFisicas`, `ISRMorales`, the three cut-offs of §11) and `TasasEfectivas.ado` l. 34–44 (`LIF … by(divSIM)`: `ISRAS`, `ISRPF`, `ISRPM`). There is no anchor to the CSI. 2. *Mechanism.* The LIF (and the ITAN) classify ISR by **who remits it**: withholding on wages 1,254.807, PF 76.665, PM 1,271.053 and withholding on non-residents 81.969 (ITAN 4T 2024; note 2_/: “the information is provided by the withholding agent and not by the person liable for payment”). The CSI classifies D.5 by **who bears it**: S.14 pays 1,540.050 (D.51 1,518.912 + D.59 21.138) and S.11 + S.12 1,188.648. The difference (D.51 S.14 − wages − PF = 187.4; with D.59, 209.2) is household ISR that the LIF records under “personas morales” (legal entities) or under withholding because a corporation remits it: withholding on interest and dividends and the ISR of PF with business activity withheld by third parties. It is not vintage: total LIF ISR 2,682.265 vs D.51 S.1 2,684.588 (+2.323). 3. *Since when.* Anchor to the LIF since v5.3 (`36b86b1`, 2022-08-30, `by(divSIM)`); it is a classification decision, not a bug. 4. *How much it weighs.* **209.212 bn** in the Σ S gap of NTA (direct τ⁻ of households underestimated); **0 in `output.txt`** today (LIF anchors). If anchored to D.51 S.14: factor 1.1413 on ISRAS + ISRPF (1,330.838 → 1,518.912) and, to balance the total, ISR PM 1,351.427 → 1,165.676 (D.51 S.11 + S.12); `INGRESOS` remains the LIF 2027, `INCD*` changes through the wage-earner/PM mix. 5. *Correction.* Decision 8 (anchor D.51 S.14 with the row “LIF vs CSI by sector” declared). **Methodological** (parameter + FLAG; `baseline`); 8.16b, with 8.17 for the Sankey.

columnas: Why Mexico solves it this way

INEGI publishes the breakdown by purpose only for “households and ISFLSH” in the territory (BIE); the CSI separates S.14 from S.15 only in the P.3 total. That is why the anchor by item is households + ISFLSH and the correction to S.14 is a single factor

texto: Purpose (provenance: this header): Precache — produces the cache of what is invariant to the scenario (v8.12 phase 2a).

Profile of the web “Calcular” flow (02_governance/perf/perfil-web-2026-10-18.md): of ~32 s, ~12 s went into pieces that do NOT depend on any form input and were recomputed on every click. This command computes them ONCE per batch run (SIM.do §5.1b, after PEF and before GastoPC, with master/ and the *RECprom already built) and saves them as a product in users/$id/cache/. The consumers (PEF, cache / GastoPC, cache / FiscalGap) read them with _precache_usa, which aborts with a recipe if they are missing or stale (no fallback). They travel to the VPS with publicar-vps.sh (Phase 3b-bis, together with the *RECprom).

Inputs — Requires: $SIMROOT, $id, $bootstrap; master/PEF.dta, master/perfiles<aniope>.dta, master/<anioenigh>/households.dta and the <var>RECprom.dta of users/$id/bootstraps/$bootstrap/. (Note: in Stata comments never write slash+asterisk: it opens a block comment and swallows the rest of the file. And the tabs of the seal are written with _tab: Stata turns tabs in the source code into spaces.)
Outputs — Items and naming convention (users/<id>/cache/):

PEF_<by>_<ifkey>.dta          annual collapse of master/PEF.dta as FiscalGap requests it (PEF if transf_gf == 0, by(divCIEP)): gasto, gastoTOT, CuoTOT in current PESOS by anio × divCIEP × transf_gf. The % of GDP is computed afterwards with pibY (it depends on CRECPIB/CRECDEF). The key is built by PEF.ado (_PEF_cachekey) from its by() and if: the same one to produce and to consume.
GastoPC_base_<aniope>.dta     the GastoPC micro data after §2 (perfiles<aniope> + households + indicators alum_/benef_/der_/pens_/ cuidados/pob), and
GastoPC_base_<aniope>_mat.dta the population COUNT matrices of §2 (tabstat [fw=factor]): matrix, column, name, value.
REC_<var>.dta                 collapse estimacion contribuyentes, by(anio modulo aniobase) of users/<id>/bootstraps/<B>/<var>RECprom.dta (what FiscalGap §4.2/§5.2 collapsed 24 times per click).

sello.txt                     tab-separated. Lines: sello  <key>  <value>      (version, data_updated, baseline, commit, generado, id, bootstrap, aniope) item   <item>   <file> insumo <item>   <path relative to SIMROOT>  <bytes>  -
Usage: Precache [, ANIOpe(int) ANIOvp(int)]    (defaults: scalars anioPE / aniovp)

texto: Purpose (provenance: 03_help/Stata/SHRFSP.sthlp “Descripción”): `SHRFSP` downloads and analyzes Mexico's public debt in its broadest measure, combining the SHCP Estadísticas Oportunas (debt stocks, financing requirements, fiscal balance and cost of debt) and the BIE (GDP and deflator). texto: Purpose (provenance: lines 2–3 of this header): profile, incidence, life cycle and projection of a per capita variable, with a bootstrap by sample design (PSU within stratum) in Mata; the five output files (PC, PERF, INCI, CICLO, REC) are read by Perfiles.ado, FiscalGap.ado and CuentasGeneracionales.ado.

tablas.titulo: Derived from the code: manifest assets (ensure_asset) and products of other modules (use master/)

texto: Procedure — METHODOLOGICAL NOTE (bootstrap, v2.0) ----------------------------------- What it computes per replicate: the total (REC), contributors (FOR), population (POB) and per capita value for a 40-year-old man; the profile by age and sex (PERF); the incidence by household decile (INCI); the life cycle sex×age×decile (CICLO) and the demographic projection of the total (REC, with the CONAPO populations). They are weighted sums by group: in Mata each replicate costs milliseconds. Up to v1.x each replicate ran PERF/INCI/CICLO/REC as programs with preserve/collapse/restore over the full database (~4 s per replicate on a database of 217 variables; B=100 × 20 variables ≈ 2-3 h). The five output files keep their schema because Perfiles.ado, FiscalGap.ado and CuentasGeneracionales.ado read them.

Resampling unit (cluster()): the ENIGH samples dwellings in PSUs (UPM) within design strata (upm, est_dis in concentrado.dta). Default `cluster(upm)`: within each stratum as many PSUs as it has are drawn with replacement, and each person's weight is multiplied by the number of times their PSU was drawn (this is what `bsample, strata(est_dis) cluster(upm)` does). If the database lacks upm/est_dis they are taken from raw/ENIGH/<anio>/concentrado.dta; if that does not exist either, it falls back to `cluster(hogar)`. `cluster(persona)` is what v1.x did (`bsample _N`): resampling individuals ignores that the persons of a household go together and underestimates the variance.

Inference: the point estimate is that of the FULL SAMPLE (original weights; replicate 0, which is not saved in the files); the standard error is the standard deviation of the B replicates; the 95% CI is reported as normal (±1.96·SE) and percentile (2.5, 97.5). Up to v1.x the point estimate was the mean of the replicates and the "CI" came from `ci means` over them: that is the interval of the MEAN of the replicates (width ∝ sd/√B), which shrinks with B and tends to zero — it underestimated the interval by a factor of √B (3.2× with B=10, 10× with B=100).

texto: Procedure — WHAT IT DOES (unification, not invention — the methodology is that of TasasEfectivasMicro.ado):
1. If the national micro/micro mirror (scalars *TEnac) does not exist, it computes it once
(TasasEfectivasMicro without entidad()): it is the reference for Rel<IMP>TE<suf>.
2. TasasEfectivasMicro, anio(<anio>) entidad(<INEGI code>) sufijo(<abbreviation in lowercase>)
— the engine speaks name (global entidad), the command speaks code (SIMentidad catalog).
3. Sample seals, like the other state products (rule P5 of SankeySF.do):
n = persons in the state's SAMPLE in master/perfiles<anio>.dta (unweighted);
per tax, top1 = % of the numerator (Σ tax × factor) contributed by ONE single person;
seal = 1 if n < sello_n (100) or top1 > sello_top1 (25 %). It is declared, not smoothed.
4. Writes users/$id/<ABREV>/tasas-efectivas.json with the command's scalars (amounts,
bases, rates, differences vs the official macro/macro TE and vs the national mirror), the
seals and the provenance. The scalars stay live in the session (escalar).

WHAT IT IS NOT: it is not additive (they are rates). What is additive are the AMOUNTS (Rec*, Base*, Pob): Σ over the 32 states = national, because TasasEfectivasMicro sums [aw=factor] by residence over the same post-adjustment base. Hence the proposed consistency gate (FLAG v8.13a): the national rate is reproduced as the average of the 32 weighted by their base.
Procedure — INHERITED DEFINITION (SIM.do §7.1–7.3; Simulador.ado):
neto   = AportacionesNetas = ImpuestosAportaciones − Transferencias, per person, [fw=factor]
aporta = ImpuestosAportaciones = ISRPM + ISRAS + ISRPF + CUOTAS + IVA + IEPSNP + IEPSP + ISAN + IMPORT
(*_Sim variables; FMP_Sim and OTROSK_Sim do NOT enter)
recibe = Transferencias = Pensiones (already with Pensión_AM, §7.2) + IngBasico + Educacion + Salud
+ OtrasInversiones (OtrosGastos and Energia do NOT enter)
celda  = five-year age group (0-4, 5-9, …, 105-109, 110+) × sex × group of NATIONAL deciles
(Deciles I-V, VI-IX, X), as in graphpiramide (grupo_edad 1..23 and over 1..3)
national unit = percentage of the NATIONAL TOTAL of net contributions: Σ of the 132 cells
= 100 (graphpiramide: POR = neto/Σneto*100; output.txt writes it with %8.3f, from the
highest five-year group to the lowest, one vector per sex × group)
present value: Simulador.ado divides the variable by the deflator of anioPE relative to anioVP
BEFORE saving aportaciones.dta (the variable already comes in pesos of anioVP; with
anioVP = anioPE the deflator is 1). aporta and recibe are deflated here with the same
ratio so that neto = aporta − recibe also holds when anioVP != anioPE.
Outputs (provenance: this header; runbook §13; 05_scripts/generar-entidades.py meta): per state, in users/$id/<ABREV>/:
§1  Poblacion if entidad == "<nombre>"          (scalars pobtot<ABREV>…; pyramid)
§2  PIBDeflactor if entidad == "<nombre>"       ONLY if master/PIBDeflactor<ABREV>.dta exists (building it downloads BISE series with a token: not done here; "sin base" + recipe is recorded)
§8.2 SankeySF.do × 5 breakdowns (state quintile, grupoedad, sexo, rural, escol), with a band of
vintages if the databases users/$id-v{2016..2024}/aportaciones.dta exist ("" ) and without it ("0")
§8.2 CicloEntidad.do                           ciclo-vida.json
§4.7 TasasEfectivasEntidad.do                  tasas-efectivas.json (TasasEfectivasMicro)
§4b  (v8.13.0) net life-cycle balance / PIBE IN STATA:  neto-pibe.json (scalarjson): NetoCicloPIBE<ABREV> =
NetoCiclo<ABREV> (record from CicloEntidad.do) / pibY<ABREV> (PIBDeflactor by state) x 100, with
NetoCiclo, Aporta, Recibe, Pob and pibY of the state; only if there is a PIBE base. And at the end of the loop,
users/$id/entidades-pibe32.json: pibYSum32 (sum of the 32 pibY<ABREV>), pibeDiscrepancia32 (% vs national
pibY) and NetoCicloPIBNac (national net / national GDP). This is what the page /entidades/<ABREV>
shows as product 4 together with the note on the discrepancy: generar-entidades.py meta only transcribes it
(rule: no number on the page is born outside Stata).
Outputs — OUTPUT: users/$id/<ABREV>/ciclo-vida.json (plain JSON, not a FusionCharts script), with:
totals (state and national), parameters, provenance and, per five-year age group × sex cell:
n      persons in the state's SAMPLE in the cell (unweighted)
pob    expanded population (Σ factor)
aporta, recibe, neto   pesos of anioVP (Σ variable × factor)
pct    % of the STATE's total net (Σ cells = 100)
pct_nac % of the NATIONAL total net (Σ over the 32 states, cell by cell = APORT* of output.txt)
top1_aporta, top1_recibe  % of the cell's aporta (recibe) contributed by ONE single person
sello  1 if n < 100 or top1_* > 25 %: rule P5 of SankeySF.do; the cell is DECLARED
thin or concentrated, not smoothed
grupos breakdown by group of deciles (same fields, without top1)
The grid is complete (23 five-year groups × 2 sexes × groups): cells without sample go with
n = 0 and zeros, they are never omitted (no silent gaps).

Series: groups of NATIONAL deciles I-V / VI-IX / X, like the national one (local grupos = "decil"; the code keeps "quintil" = STATE quintile and "ninguno" = a single series in case it is decided to change). Seals: n < 100 persons per five-year group × sex cell, top1 > 25 %.

cap0.titulo: `/metodo` — Chapter 0: Requirements for replicating the simulator
cap0.intro: *Published at `/metodo/cap0` since v8.18.0 (session 8.18); the page shows the “Other country” column empty and the Colombian candidate stays in this document. Mexican precedent for the survey–SCN adjustment: del Castillo Negrete (CEPAL, 2023), §0.7. Draft for the Colombia team. Each row is born in section 9 of a module chapter. Three columns: how Mexico solves it → what is needed generically → Colombian candidate. The Colombia column is a starting point: **everything marked ⚠ must be verified by the local team** (names, periodicity, access to microdata, departmental level).*

bloques.texto: A module is replicated if **all** its rows have an equivalent at the same level of disaggregation (person, single year of age, sex, subnational unit). If a row has no equivalent, there are three ways out, in order of preference: (a) an alternative source at the same level; (b) a declared imputation with a red seal; (c) the module is not replicated and the absence is documented. It is never filled in silently.

bloques.nota: The “Other country” column is published empty for whoever replicates to fill in; the candidate in the source document (02_governance/metodo/cap0-requerimientos.md) is not published.

secciones.titulo: 0.4 What Mexico lacks and Colombia has (advantages when replicating)

bloques.texto: - An **official** health spending profile by age (UPC by age group): Mexico imputes it. - Income and spending in a single survey (ENPH): avoids *matching*, at the cost of age. - Subnational unit with a more rule-based transfer regime (SGP by formula): eases the incidence of territorial spending.

- A recent income survey **with spending** (the GEIH does not include it): a mandatory design decision before starting (row 3). - Age profile of pensioners and contributors in RAIS (private funds): a possible red seal in pensions (row 9). - Lag of departmental accounts (row 5): the subnational unit may end up one year behind the national one.
